items.title: Australia to launch AI safety regulator after OpenAI breach | AP News
items.summary:
Tech

SECTIONS Artificial IntelligenceSocial Media  

TOP STORIES 
       Staff at the US center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns
       Anthropic is rapidly accelerating AI development amid slowdown calls, outside research group says
       Milei pitches Patagonia for AI data centers as resistance grows in the US and Europe

   
Lifestyle

SECTIONS Food & RecipesGardeningFashionHomesTravelPets [...] The regulator would enforce world-leading legislated AI standards that would apply to all frontier AI companies that want to operate in Australia, Albanese said. Financial penalties would apply, although the government has yet to detail those penalties. [...] close dialog

Australian government documents define frontier AI as the most sophisticated models at the cutting edge of current technological capability.

Albanese told OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman that the U.S. company took too long to inform the government in September that a rogue agent had infiltrated government websites three months earlier, which was the first occurrence of such a breach with the technology.

items.title: Does AI Extend or Diminish Us? | News | shorelinemedia.net
items.summary:
Flierl explained that AI is already embedded in everyday life, from electricity and water systems to navigation and financial services. While AI can help improve hurricane forecasting, support cancer research and assist with complicated mathematical problems, Flierl cautioned that excessive reliance on it can weaken critical thinking, reduce long-term learning and diminish people’s sense of meaning and ownership in their work. [...] Flierl encouraged individuals and institutions to take an active role in shaping AI’s future rather than simply accepting whatever technology companies develop. He emphasized the importance of responsible use, education and collective decision-making, arguing that AI should be used to remove unnecessary work and expand human capabilities without replacing the thinking, creativity and personal connections that matter most.

On a slide from his presentation, Flierl quoted. [...] “It’s not the AI that’s the problem… it’s the wrong use of AI.” — Michael Gerlich, as quoted in The Chronicle of Higher Education, “The Student Brain on AI”

Flierl had conducted his own research into his slides. The presentation includes several studies, surveys and company-reported discoveries;

After the presentation there was an open Q&A session with audience members asking questions.

items.title: Google faces mounting backlash for controversial AI school policy - CBS News
items.summary:
Markey is asking Alphabet if Google will commit to allowing schools to turn off AI features and chatbots in K-12 student accounts while still allowing students to access Google Search. He also requested that Google disclose any research it has conducted on the impact of its AI tools on students' mental health.

Markey has requested that Google disclose any research or testing it has conducted on the safety of its AI functions and their impact on the mental health of K-12 students. [...] Google maintains that its policy change gives schools more control over how they allow AI into schools. An Alphabet spokesperson also told CBS News that Google's AI features are now so tightly integrated into search that it cannot offer the latter without also enabling the AI services. [...] Google faces mounting public pressure to change a new policy that would limit U.S. students' access to the internet giant's widely used search platform unless schools also offer its artificial intelligence-based education tools.

In a letter to Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai on Monday, Sen. Edward Markey demanded that Google's corporate parent reverse the policy, which blocks search for K-12 student accounts that don't also provide access to apps such as Google Classroom.

items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick pointed to a recent visit to the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, where he built an AI tool that cut the time it takes to execute a particular cyber operations workflow from 100 hours to 15. That tool is now available to all cyber officers across the department, he said.

“We don’t do policy shops. We don’t do PowerPoints. We go to the edge and build with the warfighter,” he said. “You can’t be building agents from the Pentagon.” [...] He urged others across the military to adopt his hands-on approach to AI integration, encouraging troops to partner with AI experts to learn cutting-edge techniques and to tap innovative service members as in-house AI gurus who can spread that knowledge further.

        Sign up for our daily newsletter so you never miss a beat on all things federal

items.title: From scans to scribes, Yale medical faculty talk AI use in healthcare | Yale Daily News
items.summary:
Normally, diagnosing prostate cancer includes a blood test, MRI imaging and a formal diagnosis from a radiologist, who might read the same MRI image differently on different days.

Now, Onofrey said, he and other researchers are training deep learning models on these images to look for diseases including prostate cancer, though he said researchers have not validated models in large enough settings for clinical adoption yet. [...] Technology companies will face skepticism, according to Papademetris. Many AI models remain “black box” models, meaning users do not know the details of the inner workings behind the AI used in practice.

Though scientific advancement is exciting, Papademetris cautioned about implementing AI into healthcare without the proper guardrails in place. [...] Some provider systems, such as Yale Health, have incorporated AI scribes to help draft notes from patient visits. Yale researchers and professors spoke to the News about their experiences with AI-powered tools. Xenophon Papademetris, a professor at the School of Medicine, said people should be skeptical of AI use in everyday clinical practice.
